title: The approval gate: low-risk pass-through and high-risk interception

events.label: Task delegated
events.detail: "Clean the test rows out of the orders database, then send the monthly report to operations." — the first action is low-risk; the second is an outward, irreversible send.

events.label: Plan drafted
events.detail: Two actions: delete_test_rows() and send_report(). The plan goes through the gate's allowlist policy first.

events.label: Low-risk pass-through
events.detail: delete_test_rows matches the allowlist (test_ prefix only, cap 1000 rows) → auto-approved, invisible to the user — pass-through is not exemption; logging continues.

events.label: Cleanup executes
events.detail: 312 test rows deleted; the external system reports success.

events.label: Request: send_report(to=whole company)
events.detail: The second action: an outward send — spending money, external sends, modifying external data, irreversible operations: these four classes must pass a human.

events.label: High-risk interception
events.detail: The interception point is before execution: send_report is not on the allowlist → request parked, loop paused, human notified. Nothing has happened in the external world yet — that is the entire meaning of the gate.

events.label: Approval request delivered
events.detail: The request shows: action name, parameters (recipients = whole company), blast radius, and the agent's reasoning — humans need judgeable information, not a bare 'confirm?'.

events.label: Rejected with reasons
events.detail: "Wrong recipients — it should go to operations only; and the numbers need a manual check first." — rejection is also input.

events.label: Feedback fed back
events.detail: The rejection enters context as an Observation and the trajectory changes — approval is not a boolean, it is a feedback channel with reasons.

events.label: Plan revised
events.detail: Recipients switched to operations; one step added: numbers pass a validation tool before sending.

events.label: Second request
events.detail: Changed parameters make it a new request that walks the gate again — never auto-approve because 'it was rejected last time'.

events.label: Human approves
events.detail: Still outside the allowlist → notify the human; after checking recipients and numbers, the human approves. The gate records: who approved, when, on what basis.

events.label: Sent, delivered
events.detail: The report reaches operations. The audit chain is complete: every request, rejection, and approval on record — approval is not liability immunity; logs and explainability are the audit prerequisites.
